tex_content.html:
Let ${\bf K},{\bf r},\Delta $ be supplied by Theorem 5, and let $\overline\delta (t)\leq \Delta $ be positive and nonincreasing. If $M$ is a compact $3$-manifold with no $\Ar P^2$ having trivial normal bundle, then some normalized metric $g(0)$ on $M$ is the initial metric of an all-time Ricci flow with surgery satisfying Assumptions (1)--(7), positive pinching, ${\bf K}$-noncollapsing, and the strong canonical-neighborhood assumption. Surgeries in $[T_i,T_{i+1})$ use $\overline\delta (t)$ and $r_{i+1}$.

Proof

\sketch ↗ thm:main-existence-ricci-flow-surgery ↗ prop:normalized-flow-short-time-bounds Scale any metric on $M$ to make it normalized. Claim 0.1 provides the initial interval and constants; Theorem 5 extends it inductively for all time. The hypothesis on $\Ar P^2$ gives Assumption (1).

□

Lemma
[Surgery preserves Assumptions (1)--(7) and curvature pinching]

\label{RFSexists}
Let ${\bf K},{\bf r},\Delta$ be supplied by Theorem~\ref{MAIN}, and let
$\overline\delta(t)\leq\Delta$ be positive and nonincreasing. If $M$ is a
compact $3$-manifold with no $\Ar P^2$ having trivial normal bundle, then some
normalized metric $g(0)$ on $M$ is the initial metric of an all-time Ricci flow
with surgery satisfying Assumptions (1)--(7), positive pinching,
${\bf K}$-noncollapsing, and the strong canonical-neighborhood assumption.
Surgeries in $[T_i,T_{i+1})$ use $\overline\delta(t)$ and $r_{i+1}$.
\end{corollary}
